topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing for the lecture, connecting with practical sessions and outlining the learning objectives.

topics.label: Tumor Virology and Assays for Cellular Transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming tumor viruses revealed that oncogenes originate from cellular genes and established experimental assays to measure cellular transformation.

topics.label: Classification and Mutation Mechanics of Oncogenes and Tumor Suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the functional definitions of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes, illustrating their effects on cell cycle checkpoints and the consequences of different mutation types on protein activity.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Cellular Consequences of Genetic Instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the nature of sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer, detailing how defects in DNA repair pathways, replication machinery, and mitotic chromosome segregation generate genome instability.

topics.label: Multistep Tumorigenesis, Hereditary Cancer Predisposition, and Tumor Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the stepwise model of mutation accumulation in cancer development and how inherited germline mutations and subsequent clonal evolution shape disease progression.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Recommended Reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with closing remarks, recommended reading, and a preview of the next session.
